en.commentary:
I rank cordless drills by the thing that actually costs you money, which is the battery platform you marry on day one. The drill itself is a $129 to $259 decision. A five-tool build with four batteries and two chargers runs $700 to $1,400, and every one of those dollars is locked to one battery shape. That is why DeWalt's 20V MAX XR DCD805 takes the top spot at $199 bare. It sits on the widest retail footprint in the category, stocked at Amazon, Home Depot and Lowe's, and 20V MAX carries over 300 tools, so the odds that whatever you need in three years already runs on your battery are as high as this market gets.

Milwaukee's M18 FUEL 2904-20 is the better drill. It is the most compact 1/2 in. hammer drill here, it holds torque best under sustained load, and M18 has the deepest professional catalog on the market. It lands second because it is Home Depot exclusive in the US and its batteries carry the highest cost per amp-hour of any major platform, roughly $13 per Ah on a 5.0Ah pack against about $4 per Ah on Ryobi. Across a ten-tool build with six packs, that spread is worth more than the drill.

Ryobi ONE+ HP at $129 bare and $179 with a battery is the right answer for a drill that sees weekend duty. It has over 300 tools, the cheapest packs in the category, and the HP brushless motor pushed its 750 in-lbs and 31,000 BPM into the same conversation as the pro platforms.

On timing my position is firm: buy now. Power tools under HTS 8467.11 carry a 34% US tariff in 2026 against 0% before 2025, and lithium-ion packs for cordless tools carry a separate 54% line stacked on top. Stanley Black & Decker absorbed roughly $800 million in tariff cost and has already pushed high-single-digit increases through DeWalt and Craftsman this year, with more scheduled. Batteries are the part of your kit most exposed to that second tariff layer, and they are also the part you will keep buying. Waiting raises your entry price and raises the price of every pack you add after it.

highlights.title: The battery platform is the real purchase, and it costs five times what the drill does
highlights.body: Run the math the way an actual tool collection accumulates. A drill, an impact driver, a circular saw, a reciprocating saw and an oscillating tool, bare, plus four batteries and two chargers. On Ryobi ONE+ HP that build lands near $700. On DeWalt 20V MAX XR it lands near $1,000. On Milwaukee M18 FUEL it lands near $1,350, and batteries account for most of that gap. Push the same exercise to ten tools and the ordering holds, though Milwaukee's per-tool marginal cost converges because its bare-tool pricing is competitive once you already own packs. The number that decides your next five years is the total, and every comparison that stops at the drill is answering a question nobody actually has.

highlights.title: Brushless is a hard filter in 2026, and it is the one spec worth refusing to compromise on
highlights.body: Brushed motors still occupy a large share of the discounted kits that surface every holiday weekend, and they are the single most common way a budget buyer ends up with a tool they replace in two years. Brushless motors deliver more torque per amp-hour, run cooler, and carry no wear part that grinds itself down. Every drill on this page is brushless, and that is deliberate. If a kit's price looks too good for its tool count, check the motor before you check anything else, because the discount is usually coming from there.

highlights.title: DeWalt is the safest platform bet and Milwaukee is the better tool, and those are different questions
highlights.body: Milwaukee wins on hardware. The 2904-20 is shorter front to back, its REDLINK electronics hold output more consistently as the pack drains, and M18 covers professional trades that no other platform matches. DeWalt wins on access. Its tools are on the shelf at three national retailers instead of one, its batteries undercut Milwaukee's by roughly a third per amp-hour, and 20V MAX has over 300 tools including the consumer-priced ATOMIC line that lets someone enter the platform for $119. If you are a tradesperson buying on a truck account, take the Milwaukee. If you are a homeowner who wants the next tool to be easy to buy, take the DeWalt.

highlights.title: The 34% tool tariff stacks on a separate 54% battery tariff, so your packs move before your tools do
highlights.body: These are two independent lines. Power tools under HTS 8467.11 sit at 34% in 2026 against 0% before 2025, and lithium-ion cells for cordless tools carry 54% on their own schedule. Batteries are a large share of any kit's landed cost, which means the second layer hits kits harder than bare tools and hits spare packs hardest of all. The practical instruction that follows is specific: if your build needs four batteries, buy all four now. Stanley Black & Decker is moving China production below 5% by the end of 2026 and shifting capacity to Mexico over 12 to 24 months, so DeWalt's medium-term exposure improves. That relief arrives after the packs get expensive.

highlights.title: Starter kits hide their cost cutting in the battery, so read the amp-hours before the tool count
highlights.body: A two-tool kit at $169 and a two-tool kit at $229 often ship the same motors. The difference is a pair of 1.5Ah or 2.0Ah packs against 4.0Ah packs. Small packs are fine on a drill and they sag badly on a circular saw or a reciprocating saw, which is exactly what a buyer adds next. Ridgid's kit at $199 with a 4.0Ah pack and the Lifetime Service Agreement is the outlier worth naming here, because registering within 90 days makes replacement batteries free for life, and free batteries reverse the entire platform-cost calculation this page is built on.

zh-tw.commentary:
老實說，買電鑽這件事在台灣被講得太複雜了。扭力幾磅、轉速幾段、有沒有無刷，這些規格網路上抄來抄去，但真正決定你三年後會不會後悔的只有一件事，就是你選了哪一個電池平台。

一支電鑽四千到一萬，聽起來還好。你想想，等你陸續補了衝擊起子、圓鋸機、軍刀鋸、砂輪機，加上四顆電池兩個充電器，這一整套下來是三萬到五萬的規模，而且全部綁死在同一種電池上。換陣營等於整套重買，所以第一支買錯的代價遠高於單機那兩千塊的價差。

在台灣我把 Makita 放最前面，理由很直接，就是通路。DHP486 公司貨空機大概五千三，附兩顆 5.0Ah 電池的套裝落在一萬出頭。這個價格放到國際比較裡並不算漂亮，但台灣的關鍵在於全台五金行幾乎都吃牧田，夾頭鬆了、碳刷該換了、電池不進電了，騎車十分鐘就有店家收，公司貨的保固管道也最清楚。這件事在國外榜單上完全看不出來，卻是台灣使用者三年後最有感的差別。

Bosch 排在後面一點，維修據點密度僅次於牧田，GSB 系列那個卡鑽瞬間斷電的 KickBack Control 是真的有用，你在紅磚牆上打孔卡住過一次就懂。Milwaukee 在台灣走專業工具通路，工具陣容最深，但一般家庭想加買一顆備用電池得專程跑一趟，這個摩擦成本在台灣比在美國明顯很多。

至於預算有限該怎麼買，我的建議是先確認無刷，再看電池顆數。Ryobi 的電池單價是全場最低，同樣預算下你能多買兩顆電池，這對週末在家組櫃子、鎖層板的使用情境來說比多五十磅扭力有用太多。

最後講一句立場明確的，電動工具請買公司貨。BSMI 檢驗、鋰電池品質、壞掉能修，這三件事水貨都給不了你，省下的兩三千在第一次送修就賠回去了。

highlights.title: 你買的是一整套電池家族，價格是電鑽本體的五倍
highlights.body: 照真實的工具累積順序算一次就懂了。電鑽、衝擊起子、圓鋸機、軍刀鋸、磨切機五支空機，加四顆電池兩個充電器。這一套在 Ryobi 大概三萬出頭，在 Makita LXT 落在四萬上下，在 Milwaukee M18 會逼近五萬五，而且拉開差距的主要是電池不是工具本體。把規模推到十件工具，排序不會變，只是 Milwaukee 的每件邊際成本會收斂，因為你已經有電池之後它的空機價其實有競爭力。決定你未來五年花多少錢的是這個總數，只比單支電鑽扭力的評測，回答的是一個沒有人真正在問的問題。

highlights.title: 2026 年買電鑽，無刷是硬性門檻，這一項不要妥協
highlights.body: 市面上還有大量便宜的有刷套裝在流通，週年慶跟雙十一的時候特別多，這是預算讀者最常踩的坑。無刷馬達在同樣一顆電池下扭力更大、溫度更低，而且沒有碳刷這種會自己磨損的耗材。這頁上每一支都是無刷，這是刻意的篩選結果。看到一組套裝的價格相對它的工具件數好得不像話，先翻規格看馬達，八成折扣就是從那裡來的。

highlights.title: 台灣選電鑽先看維修據點，這件事的權重高於扭力
highlights.body: 美國榜單會把 Milwaukee 跟 DeWalt 放在前面，因為那邊 Home Depot 跟 Lowe's 到處都是。台灣的現實不一樣。牧田在台灣的五金行滲透率最高，Bosch 次之，這兩個牌子壞了你有地方送。Milwaukee 走專業通路，DeWalt 的實體點相對零散，你如果只是要在家裡鎖個層板、打幾個壁虎，卻買了一支要寄修的機器，那個等待期會讓你下次直接放棄修理。真正該問的問題是你家附近三公里有沒有店家收這個牌子。

highlights.title: 套裝的成本都藏在電池裡，先看安培小時再看送幾件
highlights.body: 一組四千五的雙機組跟一組六千五的雙機組，馬達經常是同一顆，差別在附的是兩顆 1.5Ah 還是兩顆 4.0Ah。小電池裝在電鑽上沒問題，裝到圓鋸機或軍刀鋸上會掉電壓掉得很難看，而圓鋸機正好是多數人補的下一件工具。買套裝的時候把電池規格找出來，這一欄比工具件數重要。

highlights.title: 週末使用者買 Ryobi，天天上工買 Makita 或 Milwaukee，這條線很清楚
highlights.body: Ryobi 的 HP 無刷把 750 in-lbs 跟每分鐘 31,000 次敲擊做出來了，週末在家組傢俱、鑽石膏板、偶爾打個磚牆，這個規格完全夠用，而且電池便宜到你可以一次買三顆。如果你是每天靠這支吃飯的人，答案換邊，Makita LXT 跟 Milwaukee M18 的機身耐用度、重載下的扭力維持、還有維修零件取得都在另一個等級，多花的錢會在第二年回本。中間地帶很窄，大部分人其實一眼就知道自己站在哪一邊。

en.commentary: The DeWalt DCD805 holds first and platform economics is the deciding factor. You buy one drill and then you buy batteries for a decade, and the 20V MAX platform has the broadest tool selection and the most competitive battery pricing of any system here. That total cost picture matters more than a torque figure you will use twice a year. If it is your job, buy Milwaukee. The Ryobi PBLHM102 at third is the value platform and I recommend it without hesitation for homeowners, since the tool breadth is enormous and the battery cost is the lowest in the category. Makita XPH14Z at fourth has the best ergonomics of the group and the Bosch GSB18V-1330 at fifth is the precision option. Labor Day promotions running through early September regularly include combo kit discounts, and buying a kit with two batteries is almost always better value than a bare tool plus batteries later. en.commentary: You are choosing a battery platform, and the drill itself is almost incidental to that decision. Once you own four batteries and a charger, every subsequent tool purchase is constrained to that ecosystem, and switching later means replacing everything. So evaluate the platform: how many tools it covers, what bare tools cost, how battery pricing has moved over three years, and how easily you can buy batteries locally. A drill that is ten percent better on a platform with half the tool range is the wrong purchase. Tool steel content also faces the 50 percent duties applied to steel and aluminium, so platform pricing has upward pressure underneath it, and building out a kit this year costs less than spreading it into next. The DeWalt 20V MAX XR DCD805 holds first at 9.2 because the 20V MAX platform has the broadest tool range at accessible prices and battery availability is excellent everywhere. The Milwaukee M18 FUEL 2904-20 at 9.1 is the stronger individual tool with better electronics, on a platform priced higher across the board. The Ryobi ONE Plus HP PBLHM102 at 8.8 is the honest recommendation for homeowners.

highlights.title: You are buying a battery platform, so evaluate the platform
highlights.body: Once you own four batteries and a charger, every future tool purchase is constrained to that ecosystem, and switching means replacing everything. Compare tool range, bare tool pricing, three-year battery cost trends, and local availability. A better drill on a narrower platform is the wrong purchase.

highlights.title: DeWalt 20V MAX wins on range and battery availability
highlights.body: The broadest tool selection at accessible prices, with batteries stocked in essentially every hardware retailer. At 9.2 the DCD805 is an excellent drill, and the platform behind it is what makes this the right recommendation for someone building a collection over several years.

highlights.title: Ryobi is the honest answer for homeowners
highlights.body: At 8.8 the ONE Plus platform covers an enormous range of tools at prices that make owning fifteen of them realistic for a household. For work happening at weekends, breadth of affordable coverage delivers more practical value than professional-grade duty cycles ever will.

highlights.title: Steel tariffs mean building out a kit costs more next year
highlights.body: Tool steel content faces the 50 percent duties applied to steel and aluminium, and that pressure works through to retail over time. If you know you want three or four tools on a platform, buying them across this year costs less than spreading those purchases into next year.

en.commentary:
This ranking has carried a tariff outlook factor for months without stating the legal authorities behind it, and that gap needed closing. Here is the current position.

On February 20, 2026 the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, invalidating the legal basis for most duties imposed since 2025. That ruling did not end tariffs on power tools. Two other authorities carry them now.

Section 301 tariffs took effect July 24, 2026, replacing the flat ten percent Section 122 tariff that expired the previous day, with a two tier structure of ten percent for most trading partners and 12.5 percent for China, Vietnam, Thailand, Brazil and Russia, layered on top of existing Column 1 rates and any antidumping or countervailing duties. Section 232 tariffs apply at fifty percent on steel and aluminium for most countries and 25 percent on copper, and those materials sit inside every tool in this ranking.

The combined effect on HTS 8467.11 power tools is a current rate around 34 percent, up from zero before 2025. In practical terms a drill kit that was 179 dollars now sits near 240. Stanley Black and Decker confirmed a four percent price increase on DeWalt 20V MAX, FLEXVOLT and Craftsman V20 lines in its Q1 2026 earnings call, already reflected on shelves.

The DeWalt DCD805 holds first at 9.2 because platform cost dominates this decision. You buy into a battery system once and everything after that is priced by that choice.

Section 301 took effect July 24, 2026 with a two tier structure, and Section 232 applies fifty percent on steel and aluminium and 25 percent on copper. The authority changed and the cost to you did not.

In practical terms a drill kit that was 179 dollars now sits near 240, with roughly 61 dollars of the sticker price attributable to duty. Stanley Black and Decker confirmed a four percent increase on DeWalt 20V MAX, FLEXVOLT and Craftsman V20 lines in its Q1 2026 earnings call.

highlights.body: Section 232 tariffs apply at fifty percent on steel and aluminium for most countries and 25 percent on copper, and all three materials sit inside every drill in this ranking. Motors use copper windings, gearboxes use steel, housings use aluminium. That means input costs rise even for tools assembled outside the countries facing the highest finished goods rates.

A cheaper drill on an expensive or narrow platform costs more over five years than a well priced drill on a broad one. Count the tools you expect to own in five years and price the batteries before you compare drills.
